messages:
Noor Khan: hi! first-week question — I can `kubectl get pods -n sandbox` fine but `kubectl port-forward svc/my-service 8080:80 -n sandbox` gives me Forbidden. I need to test the local UI, any quick fixes? /cc @DevEx

DevEx: welcome Noor :wave: can you paste the exact error output and `kubectl config current-context`? also which kubeconfig flow did you follow (SSO/okta/service-account)?

Noor Khan: context is `redwood-sandbox`. auth via Okta SSO. error:
```
error: pods/my-service: Error from server (Forbidden): pods "my-service" is forbidden: User "user:noor.khan@redwood.com" cannot create resource "pods/portforward" in API group "" in the namespace "sandbox"
```
I can `kubectl get svc -n sandbox` and `kubectl get pods -n sandbox` but port-forward fails.

DevEx: that error is specifically the port-forward subresource permission. Port-forward uses the pods/portforward verb (a subresource) which isn't included in the default "view" role. quick checks: `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n sandbox` and `kubectl auth can-i create pods/exec -n sandbox`.

Noor Khan: `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n sandbox` -> "no"
`kubectl auth can-i create pods/exec -n sandbox` -> "no"

Samir Patel: we normally keep port-forward and exec locked down in prod-ish namespaces. For sandbox we usually allow devs to port-forward, but it looks like People Ops added you to `redwood:viewers` not `redwood:dev-sandbox`. please file the access form if you haven't already, or ping People Ops.

Noor Khan: I didn't realize there are separate team groups. filed the access request (ticket 8841) now.

InfraOps: for a day-0 unblock we can apply a temporary Role that grants the subresource verbs. Example Role + RoleBinding infra can apply: 
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: sandbox-dev-portforward
  namespace: sandbox
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods/portforward", "pods/exec", "pods"]
  verbs: ["create", "get", "list", "watch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: onboarding-noor-portforward
  namespace: sandbox
subjects:
- kind: User
  name: "user:noor.khan@redwood.com"
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: sandbox-dev-portforward
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
We typically revoke temp bindings once the Okta group is synced. Want us to apply that?

Noor Khan: yes please, that would unblock me today. thanks.

InfraOps: applied onboarding-noor-portforward in sandbox, will auto-revoke in 12h. note: we included pods/exec and pods/portforward to cover common debug flows.

Onboard Bot: access request 8841 status updated -> infra temp-binding applied (auto-revoke in 12h).

Noor Khan: confirmed! `kubectl port-forward svc/my-service 8080:80 -n sandbox` works and my local UI loads. huge thanks :tada:

Samir Patel: following up to add Noor to `redwood:dev-sandbox` Okta group so infra can remove the temp RoleBinding.

DevEx: good catch — we'll add a troubleshooting note to the quickstart: include `kubectl auth can-i create pods/portforward -n <ns>` and an example Role/RoleBinding snippet for temp dev access. also add a line explaining the port-forward subresource semantics. PR incoming. :thumbsup:
